name: Honor Win 2
gaming_notes: Esports-grade hardware: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, dual active cooling fans with RGB, a 185Hz 2K OLED with 5,000Hz touch sampling, a dedicated WIN Key and X-axis linear motor. The 10,100mAh battery plus 100W wired and 80W wireless charging keep long sessions going. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: OPPO Find X10
gaming_notes: The 3nm Dimensity 9600M with a 144Hz AMOLED and 7,150mAh battery (80W charging) is flagship-class for gaming, though the Find X10 is tuned for cameras first — no dedicated gaming triggers or active cooling. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: OPPO Find X10 Pro Max
gaming_notes: The 2nm Dimensity 9600 Pro with a 144Hz gaming mode, 7,150mAh battery and 80W charging is top-tier silicon, but this is a camera flagship first — no active cooling or gaming triggers. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Samsung Galaxy F70 5G
gaming_notes: The Exynos 1330 with a 90Hz AMOLED handles casual and mid-weight games fine at medium settings, but it is not a gaming chip — heavy titles need lowered settings and the 25W charging refills the 5,000mAh battery slowly by 2026 standards. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Tecno Spark 50s 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 6400 handles casual and mid-range games at modest settings, and the 120Hz display keeps everyday play smooth. The 6,500mAh battery is the real win for long sessions. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Samsung Galaxy A18 LTE
gaming_notes: A budget chipset and 90Hz AMOLED keep casual games smooth, but this is a longevity-first phone, not a gaming one. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: NUU N10 Plus
gaming_notes: Chipset and RAM are undisclosed, so treat this as a basics-only phone — calls, browsing and light apps, not gaming. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Nubia RedMagic 12 Pro+
gaming_notes: Purpose-built esports flagship: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 + Red Core R5 co-processor, 185Hz 1.5K OLED with 960Hz touch sampling, active liquid cooling, bypass charging for sustained peak performance, and shoulder-trigger-style game controls. The 8,400mAh battery outlasts most flagships. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Tecno Pova Curve 2 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7100 with Ice Cooling 3.0, a 144Hz curved AMOLED (2160Hz instant touch sampling) and bypass charging make this a strong mid-range gaming pick — TECNO claims 90 minutes of stable Free Fire at 60fps. The 8,000mAh battery stretches long sessions, though 45W charging needs ~82 minutes for a full refill. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: itel City 300 5G
gaming_notes: The Unisoc T8200 and a 120Hz screen handle casual titles and free-to-play games like Free Fire at modest settings, but the HD+ display, 10W charging and entry-level GPU mean it is not a pick for heavy gamers. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)
